newsitem.title: FINLAND: TOURISM GROWTH KEY FOR FINNAIR - POTILA.
newsitem.headline: TOURISM GROWTH KEY FOR FINNAIR - POTILA.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy chief executive Antti Potila said on Thursday the airline would not be successful unless tourism to Finland increased.
Few foreign airlines were keen on promoting Finland as a destination, Potila said in the text of a prepared speech at a travel industry fair.
"Finnair cannot succeed unless the company is competitive and able to bring increasing traveller flows to Finland," he added.
"Only a few foreign airlines are genuinely interested in marketing Finland as a destination," Potila said.
The trend in travel and tourism was towards bigger corporate units because bigger entities possessed greater marketing power than smaller ones.
"Success is ever more dependent on marketing power. It is small for the small, big for the big," Potila said.
"International competition is fierce on the liberalised air traffic markets, and a small airline is in a tight corner," he said.
For the Finnish travel and tourism industry as a whole, Potila said the growth outlook was favourable.
"Travel is among our most important service industries and growth prospects are good," he said, adding economists and politicians were expecting the service sector to boost employment.
"This is well-founded, but new jobs will of course not be born without growth," Potila said.
"The record size of this travel fair gives us confidence in growth and in rising demand for labour," he added.
